## Step 1: Identify $\Gamma$

The subformulas of $\Box(p \vee q) \rightarrow (\Box p \vee \Box q)$ are:
$$\Gamma = \{p,\; q,\; p \vee q,\; \Box(p \vee q),\; \Box p,\; \Box q,\; \Box p \vee \Box q,\; \Box(p \vee q) \rightarrow (\Box p \vee \Box q)\}$$

**Valuation as subsets of $W$:** Every $w \in W$ is a finite binary string starting with $0$. Then $V(p) \cap W = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 0\}$ and $V(q) \cap W = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 1\}$. (The exclusion of $\sigma = ``1"$ in $V(q)$ only removes the string $``11"$, which is not in $W$ since it starts with $1$ — so the exclusion is vacuous.)

Every world ends in either $0$ or $1$, so:

- **$p \vee q$**: true at every world.
- **$\Box(p \vee q)$**: true at every world (all successors satisfy $p \vee q$).
- **$\Box p$**: false at every world — each $w$ has successor $w1$ (ends in $1$, so $\notin V(p)$).
- **$\Box q$**: false at every world — each $w$ has successor $w0$ (ends in $0$, so $\notin V(q)$).
- **$\Box p \vee \Box q$**: false at every world.
- **$\Box(p \vee q) \rightarrow (\Box p \vee \Box q)$**: false at every world (antecedent true, consequent false).

The **only** formulas in $\Gamma$ that vary between worlds are $p$ and $q$, and they are complementary.

## Step 3: Determine $W^*$

Two worlds are $\Gamma$-equivalent iff they agree on all formulas in $\Gamma$. Since only $p$ and $q$ vary (and they are complementary), there are exactly **two equivalence classes**:

$$A = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 0\}, \qquad B = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 1\}$$

$$\boxed{W^* = \{A,\, B\}}$$

## Step 4: Determine $V^*$

$$\boxed{V^*(p) = \{A\}, \qquad V^*(q) = \{B\}}$$

## Step 5: Finest filtration

The finest filtration relation is: $[w]\, R^{\text{fine}}\, [w']$ iff $\exists\, w_0 \in [w],\, w_0' \in [w']$ with $w_0\, R\, w_0'$.

- **$A\, R^{\text{fine}}\, A$**: $00 \in A$, $000 \in A$, and $00\, R\, 000$. ✓
- **$A\, R^{\text{fine}}\, B$**: $00 \in A$, $001 \in B$, and $00\, R\, 001$. ✓
- **$B\, R^{\text{fine}}\, A$**: $01 \in B$, $010 \in A$, and $01\, R\, 010$. ✓
- **$B\, R^{\text{fine}}\, B$**: $01 \in B$, $011 \in B$, and $01\, R\, 011$. ✓

So $R^{\text{fine}} = W^* \times W^*$ — the **universal relation**.

## Step 6: Coarsest filtration

The coarsest filtration relation is: $[w]\, R^{\text{coarse}}\, [w']$ iff for all $\varphi \in \Gamma$: $w' \models \varphi \;\Rightarrow\; w \models \Diamond\varphi$.

For any world $w$, successors are $w0 \in A$ and $w1 \in B$. Computing $\Diamond\varphi$ at every world:

| $\varphi \in \Gamma$ | $\Diamond\varphi$ at any $w$ |
|---|---|
| $p$ | **True** ($w0 \models p$) |
| $q$ | **True** ($w1 \models q$) |
| $p \vee q$ | **True** |
| $\Box(p \vee q)$ | **True** (successors $\in V(\Box(p\vee q)) = W$) |
| $\Box p$ | False ($V(\Box p) = \emptyset$) |
| $\Box q$ | False ($V(\Box q) = \emptyset$) |
| $\Box p \vee \Box q$ | False ($V(\Box p \vee \Box q) = \emptyset$) |
| $\Box(p\vee q) \rightarrow (\Box p \vee \Box q)$ | False ($V(\cdots) = \emptyset$) |

Formulas true at $A$: $\{p,\; p \vee q,\; \Box(p \vee q)\}$. Formulas true at $B$: $\{q,\; p \vee q,\; \Box(p \vee q)\}$.

So the condition $w' \models \varphi \Rightarrow w \models \Diamond\varphi$ is satisfied for all pairs.

So $R^{\text{coarse}} = W^* \times W^*$ — the **universal relation**.

In the filtered model $\langle W^*, R^{\text{fine}}, V^* \rangle$ with universal $R$:
- $p \vee q$ true at both $A, B$; $\Box(p \vee q)$ true at both; $\Box p$ false at both (each sees $B$ where $p$ fails); $\Box q$ false at both (each sees $A$ where $q$ fails); $\Box(p \vee q) \rightarrow (\Box p \vee \Box q)$ false at both. ✓ This matches the original model.

$$W^* = \{A, B\} \quad \text{where } A = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 0\},\; B = \{w \in W : w \text{ ends in } 1\}$$

$$V^*(p) = \{A\}, \qquad V^*(q) = \{B\}$$
